issues.competing_evidence: Langford+22 directly measure Pspin=927.7±0.1 s and Pbeat=1003.4±0.2 s but find no orbital-frequency power; conditional beat relation gives 3.41573±0.00967 h. issues.why_it_matters: Orbital clock interpretation affects binary-period comparisons and inferred donor/evolutionary state; none of the compiled or beat-derived numbers is a directly measured orbital period.
issues.needed_action: Keep the main orbital-period field unset. Obtain/review an independent spectroscopic orbital solution or the Joshi+19 original timing paper and document exactly which sideband relation underlies any future inferred value. Do not average the estimates.

issues.competing_evidence: Competing model results include 0.59±0.05 Msun (Revnivtsev+04, primary scan inaccessible), 0.62(+0.06/−0.05) (Yuasa+10), 0.67(+0.06/−0.05) (Shaw+20), 0.72±0.05 (Suleimanov+19), 0.74±0.04 and 0.75±0.04 (Xu+19 independent estimators), 0.81±0.10 (Brunschweiger+09), plus a Hayashi+23 model-dependent lower bound >0.9 Msun. No direct dynamical mass was found.
issues.references: Revnivtsev+04_V2400Oph; Yuasa+10_V2400Oph; Brunschweiger+09_V2400Oph; Suleimanov+19_V2400Oph; XuYuLi+19_V2400Oph; Shaw+20_V2400Oph; Hayashi+23_V2400Oph
issues.why_it_matters: A single preferred mass would materially change component comparisons and could bias interpretation of accretion geometry; the values use different epochs, spectral models, line diagnostics and flow assumptions.
issues.needed_action: Retain each estimate separately with its method and uncertainty. Obtain the original Revnivtsev paper and compare the assumptions/systematics across spectral and line-redshift methods before selecting any summary value; no averaging or automatic newest-value preference.

issues.competing_evidence: Buckley+95 gives approximate optical polarized-flux B≈8 MG; Vaeth+97 cyclotron models give Bpole≈9–20 MG or 15–27 MG for another inclination/assumed accretion family; Suleimanov+19 gives Bsp=4.6±0.1 MG from hard-X-ray/corotation modeling.
